title: PhD Position in Data-driven Critical Raw Material Supply Chain Resilience
description:
Do you want to investigate the resilience of critical raw material supply chains supporting low-carbon and digital technologies? Join us as a PhD student at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, University of Southern Denmark.

The Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a three-year PhD position in data-driven critical raw material supply chain resilience.

The position will be based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, Faculty of Engineering, at the SDU Odense campus. The expected starting date is 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

Project Overview

The deployment of low-carbon technologies, electrification and digital infrastructure is increasing global demand for critical raw materials. At the same time, the production and processing of many of these materials are geographically concentrated and exposed to geopolitical, economic, environmental and logistical disruptions.

Understanding how technology development affects material demand, in-use stocks, end-of-life flows and global supply dependencies is therefore important for assessing and strengthening the resilience of critical raw material supply chains.

The PhD position is jointly funded through research projects on critical raw material supply chains and material requirements for Denmark’s climate-neutral transition. The project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment combining environmental systems analysis, supply-chain research and data science.

 

PhD Topic Description

The PhD project will develop modular and data-driven approaches for analysing critical raw material demand, supply-chain dependencies and resilience.

A central methodological contribution will be the development of transparent, reusable and reproducible computational modules for dynamic material flow analysis. The modules will support the integration of technology deployment scenarios, material intensities, product lifetimes, stocks and flows, end-of-life management, recycling, production, trade, facility and ownership data.

The developed approaches will be applied to selected technology systems, including Denmark’s wind-energy infrastructure and the rapidly expanding infrastructure supporting data centres and AI computing. These cases will be analysed within a common methodological framework to examine how infrastructure expansion and technological change influence demand for critical and scarce materials, in-use stocks, future waste flows, recycling potential and global supply-chain dependencies.

The project may also investigate overlapping material requirements and competition for materials across low-carbon and digital technologies. Particular attention may be given to supply concentration, host–by-product dependencies, trade and ownership structures, supply bottlenecks, cascading risks and potential resilience strategies.

Depending on the candidate’s academic background and the specific research questions, the project may include network analysis, geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, uncertainty analysis, machine learning and other AI-supported approaches.

The candidate will build on selected existing models, datasets and research activities in the group and further develop scientifically robust and reusable methods that improve transparency, comparability and reproducibility in material-system research.

The exact research focus and detailed PhD plan will be developed jointly with the successful candidate, taking into account the project objectives, academic background and research interests.

In addition to a PhD dissertation and high-quality scientific publications, the project is expected to produce reusable modelling methods, documented datasets and reproducible computational workflows.

 

PhD Position and Research Environment

As a PhD student, you will conduct independent research under the supervision of an interdisciplinary team, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy, resource systems and sustainability transitions.

The project connects expertise in engineering, data science, mathematics, business, supply-chain research and geological resources. The wider research environment includes competences in material flow analysis, critical raw material systems, data mining, network analysis, supply-chain science, finance, investment, ownership structures, geological resources and technology systems.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU faculties and with external research partners. It may also include participation in international conferences, research visits and collaboration with relevant industrial and public-sector stakeholders.

The PhD programme follows the Danish PhD framework and includes coursework, participation in active research environments, dissemination activities, and teaching or other knowledge-dissemination duties.

 

What We Expect

We are looking for a highly motivated, independent and collaborative candidate with a strong interest in critical raw materials, quantitative modelling, data-driven research and sustainability.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent by the time of enrolment. Relevant academic backgrounds may include engineering, industrial ecology, sustainability science, resource management, data science, computer science, applied mathematics, operations research, supply-chain management, geoinformatics, mining or geological sciences, or another relevant natural science or quantitative discipline.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

  • A solid academic foundation in quantitative analysis, system modelling, data science or related methods. 

  • Experience with programming and data analysis, preferably using Python or a similar programming language. 

  • Experience with data handling, including data cleaning, transformation, integration and exploratory analysis. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

  • The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment. 

  • Good written and spoken English. 

  • A strong interest in sustainability, critical raw materials and supply-chain resilience. 

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

  • Material flow analysis, industrial ecology or material systems modelling. 

  • Network, supply-chain or geospatial analysis. 

  • Scientific computing and reproducible research workflows. 

  • Statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, optimisation, uncertainty or scenario analysis. 

  • International trade, production facility or corporate ownership data. 

  • Critical raw materials, wind energy, digital infrastructure or data centres. 

Applicants are not expected to possess expertise in all these areas. Prior experience with material flow analysis is an advantage but is not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided according to the candidate’s background and the needs of the project.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

  • Curriculum Vitae. 

  • A motivated application describing the applicant’s research interests, relevant qualifications and motivation for applying. 

  • Documentation of academic qualifications, including bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and complete transcripts of grades. 

  • Official English translations of documents not issued in English or Danish. 

  • Two letters of recommendation. 

  • A list of publications and up to two examples of relevant publications, if available. 

  • The completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • The completed TEK form for calculation of grade-point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • Official documentation describing the grading system of the awarding university, if the degree was not obtained in Denmark. 

  • Examples of relevant thesis work, software, code repositories or other research outputs, where available. 

  • Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. The place of employment is in Odense, Denmark and preferred starting date is February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

The successful candidate will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology. The research environment conducts interdisciplinary research on the global and systemic interactions between materials, technologies, energy, the environment and society.

The Department of Green Technology is located in Odense, the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark. Odense offers an international research environment and an open Scandinavian working culture.

 

Further Information

Further information about the scientific content of the position is available from:

Wu Chen
Associate Professor
Department of Green Technology
SDU Life Cycle Engineering
University of Southern Denmark
Email: wuc@igt.sdu.dk

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

title: Student Assistant - Data & Analytics (BluePool and Data Governance)
description:
Do you want to help shape the future of Europe’s energy system and contribute to a fully carbon‑neutral, sustainable power grid? Are you a data engineer who is curious, open‑minded, and initiative-taking — someone who enjoys working in an explorative and collaborative environment? Do you want to collaborate with engineers, application developers, and data scientists to unlock insights from the vast amounts of data behind our services? 

We are looking for a Student Assistant to support our Data & Analytics department. This is an excellent opportunity for a student who wants practical experience working with data platforms, governance processes, documentation, and operational support activities in an international and highly technical environment. 

Nordic RCC – supporting security of supply and the green energy transition 

Nordic Regional Coordination Centre (RCC) provides critical services and insights to support the national Transmission System Operators (TSOs) in Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark — to ensure the efficient operation and use of the Nordic power system and high security of power supply at any time. 

Based in Copenhagen, Nordic RCC is one of six RCCs in Europe, equally owned by the Nordic region's four electricity TSOs: Fingrid, Statnett, Svenska Kraftnät, and Energinet. 

As European power systems integrate and evolve to meet climate goals, Nordic RCC provides regional coordination, integrated services, regional insights and recommendations to the Nordic TSOs and their control centres, to support cross-border operational security 24/7.  

Join Nordic RCC, a fast-developing company determined to make a significant impact in the energy sector and to provide for a secure and efficient transition to the green, sustainable energy system. 

Right now, we are looking for a Student Assistant to join our Data & Analytics Department. 

What You Will Be Working On 

The Data and Analytics team consists of 10 employees and consultants and plays a central role in enabling data-driven decision-making across Nordic RCC. The team develops and maintains data pipelines, analytics products, BI solutions, platform services, and information services that support operational, strategic, and regulatory needs. 

As Student Assistant, you will support various initiatives across the department, with a primary focus on NRCC's analytics platform ‘BluePool’, and data governance activities. 

Examples of tasks may include: 

BluePool Support 

  • Assisting with user onboarding and access administration 

  • Maintaining onboarding guides and user documentation 

  • Supporting training sessions and workshops 

  • Gathering and tracking user feedback 

  • Assisting with testing of new BluePool functionality 

Data Governance 

  • Supporting data governance processes and documentation 

  • Maintaining data catalogues and metadata documentation 

  • Assisting with data classification and governance activities 

  • Supporting compliance and process-related initiatives 

General Department Support 

  • Coordinating meetings and workshops 

  • Maintaining team documentation and knowledge bases 

  • Preparing presentations and communication materials 

  • Supporting project coordination and follow-up activities 

  • Assisting with ad hoc analytical and administrative tasks 

Who We Are Looking For 

You are currently enrolled in a relevant university programme, for example within data science, computer science, engineering, information management, business analytics, economics, mathematics, or a similar field. 

You do not need extensive professional experience. What matters most is that you are curious, structured, and comfortable taking ownership of practical tasks — from organizing documentation and following up on details to supporting colleagues with day-to-day needs. 

We are looking for someone who: 

  • Is detail-oriented and follows tasks through carefully 

  • Enjoys turning information into clear documentation, guides, or overviews that others can use 

  • Communicates clearly in writing and verbally 

  • Can work independently while also asking for input when needed 

  • Has an interest in data, analytics, and digital platforms 

  • Is comfortable using Microsoft Office tools 

It is an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have experience with one or more relevant tools or concepts, such as Python, SQL, Power BI, enterprise architecture, data governance, or technical documentation. 

What We Offer: 

  • A flexible student position that can be adapted to your studies 

  • Exposure to large-scale data and analytics initiatives within the energy sector 

  • Experience working in an international environment with Nordic stakeholders 

  • Insight into data governance, analytics platforms, and digital transformation 

  • Opportunities to build practical skills that are highly relevant for a future career in data and analytics 

  • A friendly and collaborative team with experienced data scientists, data engineers, and analytics specialists 

Application & Security Clearance 

Please apply online in English no later than 5 November 2026. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis. 

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.   

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system.  

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.  Nordic RCC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: OT Security Architect - Renewables, Location: Denmark , DK - Esbjerg, DK - Copenhagen
description:
Are you an experienced and motivated OT Security Architect and do you want to leave your mark on the global energy industry? If so, we want to hear from you! 
 
Your position
 
In your new position as OT Security Architect in the Renewables division, you will be a valuable member of the OT Security Team, whose mission is to ensure excellent OT security deliveries on large-scale EPC substation projects. You will have the chance to take the architectural lead and help shape a collaborative team culture built on expertise and knowledge-sharing. Above all, your work will make a real difference to the global energy sector.

Your place of work will be at one of our offices in either Esbjerg or Copenhagen. The position is full-time, and you can expect to travel 10–30 days per year.

“Every day, we help enable the green energy transition by building secure, resilient OT solutions that ensure renewable energy assets operate safely and reliably.” - OT Security Architect & Team Lead, Reza Sarafrazjoo.
 
Your tasks & responsibilities 

In our Renewables division, we have major EPC projects in the pipeline for both short- and long-term operations. As an OT Security Architect, you will take the architectural lead and support all OT Security areas across the EPC substation projects.

Your tasks will include but are not limited to:

  • Contributing to the implementation of industry-accepted good practice and required Cyber/OT Security architecture at solution level, typically based on standards such as IEC 62443, ISO 27001, and NIS
  • Helping define products and standards relevant to OT Security and infrastructure
  • Hands-on experience with cybersecurity audits and compliance frameworks, including ISO 27001, Critical Infrastructure regulations, and IEC 62443
  • Reviewing requirements/ITT packages and providing input to tenders consisting of calculations, solutions, descriptions, clarifications, and reservations
  • Taking on an advisory or active role in infrastructure, identity access management, or logging/event-based activities
  • Being responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing FAT, SAT, and SIT activities to ensure successful system delivery and integration
  • Implementing customer-specific Cyber/OT Security requirements in substation design for multiple systems and subsystems, such as SCADA, low-voltage, HVAC, Auxiliary Control and Monitoring System, etc.


Crucial to this position is your ability to take ownership of project deliverables and coordinate OT Security deadlines with internal and external stakeholders. You should thrive in a leading role where your skills, collaboration, and structured approach help ensure that requirements are met.
 
Your profile & qualifications

You are a team player who enjoys leading projects and working with stakeholders to align on timing, scope, and objectives. You know when technical expertise should be brought in to support delivery. To us, this means that you have a structured and solution-oriented approach, the ability to influence stakeholders, and the dedication to see tasks through to completion.

You will be part of a team of six colleagues that values quality, attention to detail, and a flexible working environment. We are sociable, helpful, and open to input, and we work in a dedicated, structured, and execution-focused way while respecting the agility that is a natural part of our core tasks. We want the same from you.

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have:

  • A minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in OT Security from a similar position
  • A Tech Lead mentality – we are not seeking an extreme subject matter expert, but a well-rounded colleague who can work through heavily structured large projects involving many stakeholders 
  • The ability to know when additional technical specialists or resources are needed to complete a project
  • Excellent communication skills and fluency in English
  • Experience working in complex engineering projects, as well as project and stakeholder management, is an advantage


If you have any questions, you are more than welcome to contact OT Security Architect & Team Lead, Reza Sarafrazjoo.
 
Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey: how to get there. We provide the answers needed to make change real, because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever, pragmatic solutions. This is what we do, and this is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.
So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

title: Chip Ecosystem Partnership and Funding Manager, The position is a Senior Advisor at TEK Innovation
description:
Do you want to help facilitate and grow the semiconductor and chip ecosystem in Denmark and beyond, working with the leading researchers in the field, and to turn potential into opportunities, partnerships and projects? Then this job could be for you.  

About the position 

SDU Microelectronics at TEK, headed by professor Farshad Moradi, is part of the Danish Chips Competence Centre (DkCCC) - the new Danish hub for chip technology and your strategic platform. The position offers an opportunity to play a central role in strengthening Denmark’s chip ecosystem and to help connect the ecosystem with fast-growing application areas such as drones, robotics, sensors and autonomous systems, where advanced chip technology is becoming increasingly critical for performance, reliability, energy efficiency and future innovation. 

You will work closely with SDU researchers, DkCCC partners, Danish universities, companies, incubators, industry organizations, funding advisers and European chip networks. Learn more here www.dkccc.eu 

The position involves regular travel within Denmark and occasional travel elsewhere in Europe. 

Your main responsibilities will include:  

  • Identifying relevant national and European funding opportunities in chip technology, semiconductor development, and chip-enabled applications. 

  • Developing and maintaining a strategic pipeline of funding calls, project ideas and potential consortium partners. 

  • Engaging proactively with Danish start-ups, SMEs and established companies to understand their technological needs and funding requirements. 

  • Connecting companies with relevant researchers, facilities and competencies at SDU and other Danish universities. 

  • Helping companies and researchers translate technical and business ideas into fundable project concepts. 

  • Initiating and facilitating Danish and European consortia for chip-related funding calls and identifying opportunities to join existing consortia. 

  • Promoting Danish chip competencies and contribute to the visibility and strategic development of DkCCC.  

  • Supporting the full process of funding applications, from project objectives and facilitating consortiums, to coordinating proposals with partners and funding advisers. 

  • Building relationships with key stakeholders, organizing activities, and events supporting the ecosystem.   

Your profile 
You have a relevant master's degree, for example within engineering or natural sciences, business development or innovation management, economics or business administration, European studies or public policy, research and innovation management, or another relevant field. 

You have documented experience in one or more of the following: 

  • National or European research and innovation funding 

  • Development of collaborative funding proposals 

  • Consortium building and partner identification 

  • University–industry collaboration or innovation/business development 

  • Supporting start-ups, SMEs or deep-tech companies 

  • Stakeholder management and professional networking 

We are looking for a colleague who: 

  • Is proactive and comfortable initiating contact with companies, researchers and potential partners.  

  • Is a strong relationship builder who can establish trust across organizational and disciplinary boundaries 

  • Understands both commercial needs and academic interests and can structure complex consortium-development processes, while maintaining momentum towards a deadline 

  • Communicates clearly with different stakeholders, technical, academia and experts, business 

  • Works independently and is persistent and solution oriented, while also contributing actively to a team 

Experience with semiconductors, microelectronics, integrated circuits, quantum technologies, photonics, sensors or other deep-tech fields is a significant advantage — though you don't need to be a chip designer. What matters more is your ability to grasp technology-based opportunities, engage technical specialists, and turn complex ideas into fundable partnerships. Knowledge of European research and innovation programs, including EU Chips Act calls, is also an advantage. 

What we offer 

  • Become part of SDU’s growing environment for microelectronics and chip technology. 

  • Build partnerships that may lead to new products, technologies, companies, and investments. 

  • Work directly with promising Danish start-ups, companies and research environments. 

  • Help create new university–industry collaborations. 

  • Develop national and European networks within a strategically important technology area. 

  • Influence the formation of projects from their earliest stages.  

  • Collaborate with leading researchers and industry specialists, in an international and interdisciplinary environment. 

  • A role with considerable independence and the opportunity to shape the methods, networks, and activities used to identify funding opportunities and develop consortia. 

Your organizational home will be TEK Innovation, the research support and innovation unit at TEK, where you will have colleagues with similar jobs, supporting emerging ecosystems, as well as funding advisors and project managers. Your academic home with SDU Microelectronics, where you will work closely with professor Farshad Moradi and his team.  

For further information about the position, please contact: 

Thit Juul Hvid, Head of TEK Innovation, The Technical Faculty at The University of Southern Denmark tjuul@tek.sdu.dk 

Professor Farshad Moradi, SDU Microelectronics, The Technical faculty at The University of Southern Denmark at moradi@sdu.dk  

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support. 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST).

First Interview: week 46, second interview, week 47.

The startdate will be January 1, 2027, or at the earliest convenience.

Salary and employment terms:  

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Employment shall take place in accordance with the framework agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Application must include cover letter, CV and exam certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

All documents must be in English and PDF format.  All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.  

You can only apply for the position at – https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/job-sdu. 

All attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. Cover letter and CV can contain max. 5 Mb.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.

title: Two-year Postdoctoral Position on Spintronics for Advanced Computing: Spintronic Device Fabrication, Characterization and Advanced Computing
description:
The Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a 2-year position as a postdoctoral researcher within spintronic computing. The position offers an exciting opportunity to advance spintronics through device physics, simulation, fabrication, experimental characterization, and integration of spintronic devices for advanced computing applications.

We are seeking a highly motivated candidate to investigate, design, fabricate, and characterize spintronic devices, with particular emphasis on Anisotropic Magnetoresistance (AMR), Giant Magnetoresistance (GMR), and Tunneling Magneto Resistance (TMR) devices. The work will combine magnetic and spintronic device physics, materials and multilayer structures, device fabrication, electrical measurement, modelling, and data analysis, with the aim of developing reliable spintronic technologies for advanced computing and emerging semiconductor applications.

The research will focus on understanding, controlling, and exploiting thermal fluctuations and stochastic switching in MTJs for physical entropy generation and energy-efficient computing, with particular emphasis on True Random Number Generators (TRNGs) and Stochastic Neural Accelerators (SNAs).

The successful candidate will work on the physics-based design, modelling, simulation, fabrication, and experimental characterization of spintronic devices and their integration into advanced computing systems. The position also includes a role in the Danish Chips Competence Center, where the candidate will contribute to connecting the Danish semiconductor and spintronics ecosystem with relevant EU pilot lines, facilitating collaboration, technology development, prototyping, and access to European semiconductor fabrication capabilities. The candidate will also contribute to preparing and writing research proposals and funding applications related to spintronics, semiconductor technologies, and advanced computing.

As a spintronic postdoc, you are expected to: 

  • Perform atomistic and micromagnetic simulations of s-MTJ structures and magnetization dynamics to investigate switching mechanisms, thermal activation, stochasticity, variability, and operating conditions relevant to TRNG and SNA applications.

  • Contribute to the electrical, magnetic, and transport characterization of fabricated AMR, GMR, and TMR devices, including resistance states, magnetoresistance, switching behaviour, current/voltage dependence, temperature dependence, and device-to-device variability, and correlate experimental results with modelling and simulation.

 

What we offer 

  • A stimulating research environment within SDU Microelectronics, a growing section integrating expertise in analog/digital IC design, spintronics, advanced computing, semiconductor technologies, and energy-efficient system architectures. 

  • Access to advanced facilities and infrastructure for spintronic device design, fabrication, electrical and magnetic characterization, and system prototyping, together with opportunities to collaborate with relevant Danish and European pilot-line and semiconductor facilities. 

  • Excellent opportunities for collaboration across SDU and with national and international academic and industrial partners in microelectronics, semiconductor technology, photonics, spintronics, and advanced computing, including activities connecting the Danish ecosystem with EU pilot lines.

  • An open and collaborative research culture within SDU’s Faculty of Engineering (TEK), The Mads Clausen Institute (MCI), promoting interdisciplinary innovation across electronics, materials science, semiconductor processing, spintronics, and artificial intelligence.

 

What we expect 

Applicants should hold a PhD in Electronic and Communication Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, or a closely related field (the degree should have been completed within the last 6 years at most): 

  • Expertise in spintronics, magnetism, magnetic device physics, or related areas, with demonstrated experience in physics-based modelling and/or simulation of magnetic or spintronic devices. Experience with s-MTJ devices, stochastic magnetization dynamics, or thermal switching is highly desirable and electrical modeling of sMTJs using Verilog to be used in Cadense

  • Experience with experimental characterization of AMR, GMR, MTJ, or related spintronic devices, including electrical and magnetic measurements, resistance and magnetoresistance characterization, switching behaviour, and data analysis. Experience with pilot-line activities, technology transfer, or collaboration with semiconductor foundries is an advantage.

  • A strong research track record demonstrated through peer-reviewed publications and the ability to work effectively in collaborative research environments. Experience in writing research proposals, funding applications, or project plans is highly desirable.

  • Team player with strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with academic, industrial, and technology-development partners across Denmark and Europe. 

All candidates must demonstrate excellent verbal and written English skills, along with very good communication abilities and the ability to communicate technical results to multidisciplinary and international partners. 

 

Workplace description 

The successful candidate will join SDU Microelectronics, a dynamic and expanding section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME). title: Two-year Postdoc position on Spintronic Quantum-inspired Computing
description:
Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a 2-year Postdoctoral Researcher position within the newly funded QUANTRONIC – Spintronic Pseudo-Qubits for Room-Temperature Quantum Computing project, supported by the Villum Experiment programme of Villum Fonden.

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate a new class of spintronic pseudo-qubits (p-qubits) based on spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs). The project explores whether engineered stochastic spintronic devices can reproduce key computational mechanisms associated with quantum systems - including superposition-like states, probability-amplitude-based interference, and entanglement-like correlations—without relying on fragile quantum coherence or cryogenic operation.

QUANTRONIC is a high-risk, high-gain research project positioned at the intersection of spintronics, probabilistic computing, quantum-inspired computing, nanoelectronics, and integrated circuit design. The central concept is a novel SOT-MTJ architecture designed to represent and manipulate probability amplitudes and to enable synchronization between multiple pseudo-qubits. The project will combine physics-based modelling, device design and fabrication, experimental characterization, and system-level demonstrations.

The successful candidate will work within SDU Microelectronics and collaborate closely with international partners, particularly INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory, on the design and fabrication of spintronic devices.

The position is expected to start in February 2027, with the specific starting date to be agreed with the successful candidate.

 

As a Postdoctoral Researcher in QUANTRONIC, your key responsibilities will include:

  • Develop and refine physics-based compact models of SOT-MTJ-based pseudo-qubits, including stochastic switching and inter-device coupling.

  • Develop Verilog-A models and integrate them into circuit-level simulation environments such as Cadence.

  • Investigate the physical requirements for controlling probabilistic states and representing probability amplitudes in spintronic devices.

  • Collaborate with project partners on the design and fabrication of SOT-MTJ devices and arrays.

  • Experimentally characterize standalone devices and coupled arrays, including stochastic switching, synchronization, and entanglement-like correlations.

  • Investigate quantum-inspired gate operations and system-level demonstrations using networks of pseudo-qubits.

  • Contribute to proof-of-concept demonstrations, including integer factorization and other quantum-inspired computational problems.

  • Publish research results in high-quality international journals and conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results.

  • Collaborate with researchers in spintronics, probabilistic computing, microelectronics, materials science, and quantum information.

 

What we offer

  • A unique opportunity to work on a high-risk, high-gain research concept exploring a new computational regime between classical probabilistic and quantum computing.

  • A stimulating research environment within SDU Microelectronics, a growing research section with expertise in spintronics, probabilistic computing, neuromorphic computing, analog/digital IC design, and emerging computing architectures.

  • Access to advanced facilities for electronic design, device characterization, measurement, and system prototyping.

  • Close collaboration with INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory on spintronic device technology and fabrication.

  • Opportunities to collaborate with national and international researchers in spintronics, quantum-inspired computing, quantum technologies, and nanoelectronics.

  • An open, international, and collaborative research environment within SDU's Faculty of Engineering, supporting interdisciplinary research across electronics, physics, materials science, and computing.

  • Strong opportunities for developing an independent research profile in an emerging area of probabilistic and quantum-inspired hardware.

 

What we expect

Applicants should hold a PhD in electronic engineering, electrical engineering, applied physics, nanotechnology, spintronics, or a closely related field.

The ideal candidate should have experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Spintronics and magnetic devices, particularly MTJs, STT-MTJs, SOT-MTJs, or related technologies.

  • Physics-based modelling of nanoscale or magnetic devices.

  • Verilog-A, SPICE, and Cadence or comparable circuit/device simulation environments.

  • Experimental characterization of electronic, magnetic, or spintronic devices.

  • Stochastic or probabilistic computing systems.

Experience in micromagnetic simulation, magnetotransport measurements, nanofabrication, probabilistic computing, or quantum/quantum-inspired computing will be considered a strong advantage.

We are particularly interested in candidates who are enthusiastic about working across traditional disciplinary boundaries and are comfortable combining device physics, modelling, experimentation, and computing concepts.

The successful candidate should be able to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary and international research team. Excellent written and spoken English and strong communication skills are required.

title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions
description:
Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
University of Copenhagen

The University seeks to appoint a tenure track assistant professor to commence 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Information on the department can be found at: http://www.sund.ku.dk/.

Subject area: Infectious disease epidemiology, modelling, animal health, One Health, and sustainable health systems

The Tenure-Track Assistant Professor will lead research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, with particular emphasis on how changes in environmental conditions, animal populations, production systems, and management practices influence disease emergence, transmission, and control. The position will combine infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical and statistical modelling, data science, and economic analysis to generate evidence supporting disease preparedness, prevention, and control.

The successful candidate will:

  • Lead independent research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, including the influence of environmental and production system changes.
  • Develop and apply simulation, epidemiological, and statistical models to assess disease and spillover risks, evaluate mitigation and control strategies, and quantify their economic implications.
  • Demonstrate strong programming skills in R and other relevant programming languages, including experience in managing, processing, and analysing large and complex datasets.
  • Have experience in developing and applying epidemiological disease-spread models, including model calibration, validation, parameter estimation, and calculation of epidemiological indicators such as the basic reproduction number (R₀) across different animal species and production systems.
  • Design and implement epidemiological modelling frameworks.
  • Validate and calibrate models using large-scale national datasets, ensuring scientific robustness, methodological validity, and relevance for policy and decision-making.
  • Translate research findings into evidence supporting risk-based disease prevention, preparedness, and control.
  • Establish and maintain collaborations with key stakeholders, including the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, industry partners such as SEGES and Landbrug & Fødevarer (L&F), and international organisations such as the FAO.
  • Lead and secure independent research funding through competitive national and international funding calls. The position requires demonstrated experience in securing external funding, as well as the ambition to develop research ideas into externally funded projects and provide scientific leadership for such projects within the TIPTON Research Group.
  • Contribute to the development and delivery of One Health and sustainability teaching, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, disease preparedness, and the interactions between animal, human, and environmental health.
  • Contribute to teaching in data science, including data management, dataset preparation and handling, statistical analysis, programming, and the analysis of large-scale and complex datasets.
  • Supervise students and contribute to research capacity building within infectious disease epidemiology, disease modelling, data science, and One Health.
  • Contribute to the delivery of government services undertaken by the Department, including research-based advice, preparedness activities, risk assessments, and other activities relevant to infectious disease modelling and control.
The position is expected to combine methodological excellence in infectious disease modelling and data science with applied epidemiological research, generating evidence that is directly relevant to disease preparedness, private and public bodies, sustainable production systems, animal health and resilient health systems.

The tenure track assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

  • research, including publication/academic dissemination
  • research-based teaching
  • sharing knowledge with society
  • participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors
The tenure track assistant professor’s performance will be evaluated through annual evaluations. Furthermore, the tenure track assistant professor will be evaluated in a mid-track appraisal.

After no more than six years of employment and on condition of a positive final appraisal, the tenure track assistant professor will be employed as associate professor. Find more information about tenure track at the University of Copenhagen.

Required qualifications
To be qualified for an assistant professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

  • a PhD degree or similar qualifications within the subject area
  • research experience within the field of the position
The tenure track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact.

The assistant professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

Salary and employment conditions
The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

The position is permanent.

Employment is as Tenure Track Assistant Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector at www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

Questions
For further information, please contact Research Group Leader: Professor Beate Conrady, bcon@sund.ku.dk

Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

Application
The application must be submitted in English, and must include the following documents:

  • Application (Including motivation for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages))
  • Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding)
  • Diplomas (Master’s, PhD and other relevant diplomas)
  • A complete list of publications
  • Research plan (2-4 pages)
  • Teaching plan
  • Uploads of maximum 5 publications to be considered in the assessment
  • Teaching portfolio, if applicable (Guidelines)
Please note: It is mandatory to upload a teaching plan in the online application form. Should you not be able to produce a teaching plan, please upload a blank document in this box instead.

Application procedure
After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

The application will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested in this post to apply.

Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, 18 November 2026.

Interviews for this position are likely to be held on 7 April 2027.

title: PhD position at the Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
description:
The Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA) at The Mads Clausen Institute, University of Southern Denmark, is seeking a talented and highly motivated PhD student to work on the development of new theoretical frameworks for describing light–matter interactions in advanced van der Walls heterostructures probed by polaritons generated through inelastic tunneling. The position is funded by a Villum Young Investigator grant awarded to Assistant Professor P. André D. Gonçalves, who will supervise the PhD research.

The position is available starting 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will develop new theoretical frameworks and computational methods to investigate the fundamental limits of polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling in tunnel junctions based on van der Waals heterostructures composed of atomically thin materials. The project will employ a broad range of analytical, semi-analytical, and numerical techniques to explore electrically driven polaritonic phenomena. A major focus will be on harnessing polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling as a tool to probe and manipulate light–matter interactions at the nanoscale, as well as to characterize the optoelectronic response of complex quantum materials.

We welcome candidates with a strong background in condensed-matter physics and/or quantum nanophotonics who are highly motivated and eager to pursue world-class research in theoretical quantum nano-optoelectronics. Experience with scientific programming is expected, while familiarity with numerical techniques is advantageous but not required. The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic about contributing to cutting-edge research in a dynamic and ambitious young research group, supported by the POLIMA Center and its extensive network of international collaborators.

POLIMA is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) for an initial period of 6 years (2023–2028), with the possibility of a 4-year extension. The center is led by Professor N. Asger Mortensen and currently consists of two Professors, three Assistant Professors, a Lab Manager, a Center Administrator, and approximately 10–15 PhD students, postdocs, and visiting scientists. Several POLIMA researchers have attracted prestigious personal grants, e.g., Villum Investigator, Villum Young Investigator, DFF Sapere Aude, Novo Nordisk’s Foundation RECRUIT and Data Science Investigator – Emerging, and Maria Skłodowska-Curie Fellowships. Read more on POLIMA’s website.

We offer a competitive and highly collaborative research environment with close interaction between experimental and theoretical activities. You will join a thriving community of researchers and benefit from a strong network of international collaborators. Our work environment is supportive, dynamic, and designed to foster creativity and the development of innovative projects.

 

We offer:

• A PhD student position in an ambitious and supportive, international research environment.

• A dedicated supervisor research team to support the academic development of the PhD student.

• Access to state-of-the-art equipment, facilities, and infrastructure.

• A competitive salary and social benefits (e.g., health coverage, parental leave, social security, etc.) (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/international-staff/getting-settled)

POLIMA is located at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense – 1h15min by train from Copenhagen Airport. The University of Southern Denmark offers dedicated assistance and support with various practical, social, and legal aspects (housing, visa, administration, tax, etc.), especially for international candidates through our international staff office (ISO) and the administrative staff at POLIMA.

 

For further information and details about the position, application, and the research center, please contact Assistant Professor Paulo André Dias Gonçalves (padgo@mci.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

  • Motivated application. 

  • Curriculum Vitae.

  • Master’s and bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (copy of original and an official English translation).  

  • Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

  • An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

  • Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

  • List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

  • References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is 31 December, 2026, at 11:59 PM / 23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process. 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

The preferred start date is 1 March 2026 (may be adjusted by mutual agreement) or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

title: FAÇADE DECORATOR / STUCCO WORKER / SPECIALIST MASON
description:
Are you an experienced craftsman with a passion for traditional craftsmanship and decorative work?

We are a Danish construction company specialising in high-end properties, historic and listed buildings, and projects that require a high level of craftsmanship and attention to detail.

We are looking for an experienced façade decorator, stucco worker or specialist mason with proven experience in decorative façade work and traditional building techniques.

The ideal candidate will have several years of experience working with cornices, mouldings, ornaments, decorative façades, stucco and detailed plasterwork, and will know how to recreate and restore decorative features with the precision and quality required when working on historic and architecturally significant buildings.

We are not necessarily looking for a traditional bricklayer. What is most important to us is that you are highly skilled in your craft and have genuine experience with decorative and ornamental work carried out using traditional methods.

We are looking for someone who:

● Has solid and documented experience in façade decoration, stucco work or specialist masonry

● Has experience working on historic, older or listed buildings

● Is experienced in traditional techniques and materials

● Has a strong eye for detail, proportions and high-quality finishes

● Is able to work independently and take responsibility for the quality of their work

● Understands and respects the original architecture of historic buildings

● Can provide professional references and preferably photographs of previous projects

What we offer

You will become part of a professional team working on exclusive and unique properties and projects where traditional craftsmanship and attention to detail are highly valued.

You will have the opportunity to work on challenging and interesting projects where your experience and specialist skills are genuinely appreciated.

Salary will be negotiated according to qualifications and experience.

If you have the experience, craftsmanship and passion for the details that make a difference, we would be very interested in hearing from you.

Please send us a short application, CV and, if possible, photographs and references from previous work.

We look forward to hearing from you and discussing the possibility of you joining our team.

Contact us for an informal conversation about the position.

Best regards, Ali

title: Autoremondilukksepp
description:
Varasem kogemus autoremondi vallas vähemalt aasta.

Tööülesanded: Meil on töökojas tõstukid, tööriistad, õli, rooste, katkised autod ja aeg-ajalt ka klient, kes vannub, et “enne teie juurde tulekut oli kõik korras”.
Kui sa ei minesta rooste peale, ei hakka nutma kinnise poldi pärast ja tead, et “kliendi sõber juba vaatas” tähendab tavaliselt uut õudusfilmi kapoti all — siis räägime. Puudu on veel üks **autoremondi lukksepp**, kes ei hakka nutma, kui polt on kinni, käsi on must või kapoti alt vaatab vastu järjekordne “kodune remont”.

Omalt poolt pakume: Meie poolt:
🔥 normaalne palk — kui oskad, siis saad ka raha; 🔥 päris töö, mitte niisama kapoti silitamine; 🔥 seltskond, kus nalja saab ja lumehelbekesed sulavad kiiresti; 🔥 tööriided, lisasoodustused; 🔥 autod, mille kallal saad oma viha seaduslikult välja elada.

Muud nõuded: Ootame sind, kui:
✅ tead, et haamer ei ole alati vägivald — vahel on see diagnostikavahend; ✅ saad aru, et “klõbin ees vasakul” võib tähendada kõike alates kondist kuni täieliku katastroofini; ✅ ei arva, et piduritoru paikamine teibiga on loominguline lahendus; ✅ oskad autot remontida nii, et see pärast ka päriselt töötab; ✅ sul on töötahe suurem kui soov reede pärastlõunal kella vaadata.

title: Breakfast Cook
description:
Work tasks: Kolm Õde boutique hotel (Pikk 71, Tallinn Old Town) is looking for a breakfast chef to join our team. Our breakfast is a buffet focused on Estonian produce and bread and pastries baked on site, and it is open to guests of the hotel and our apartments as well as to outside visitors.
Your main duties: - preparing hot and cold breakfast dishes (egg dishes, porridges, hot sides, salads, cold cuts, smoked fish, etc.); - baking bread, buns and morning pastries on site; - setting up the buffet before opening and keeping it replenished during breakfast; - taking care of the taste, freshness and attractive presentation of the food; - preparing for the next day (doughs, prep work, etc.); - monitoring stock, preparing orders and receiving deliveries; - following food hygiene and self-monitoring (HACCP) requirements, checking temperatures and shelf life; - keeping the kitchen, equipment and tools clean and in order; - working closely with the breakfast server and reception, and helping develop the menu. You are responsible for making sure every morning starts with a tasty, fresh and beautifully presented breakfast for our guests.

We offer: - Work in a unique setting: Kolm Õde boutique hotel is housed in three medieval merchant houses in the heart of Tallinn Old Town.
- The opportunity to bring your own ideas to the menu. - Morning working hours – your evenings stay free. - Work uniform. - A small, friendly team and international guests. - A central location that is easy to reach by public transport.

Other requirements: - Previous experience as a cook (experience with breakfast service, hotel kitchens or baking is a big plus).
- Valid health certificate (tervisetõend). - Willingness to work early mornings, as well as on Saturdays and Sundays. - Cleanliness, accuracy, independence and good time management. - A desire to cook tasty, beautifully presented food and to help develop our new breakfast concept.

Option to work from home: No

description:

Otsime oma meeskonda külaliskorterite koristajaid nii täis- kui osalise koormusega. Võimalik on töötada ka ainult nädalavahetustel (näiteks laupäevast esmaspäevani) — töö sobib hästi lisatööks. title: Office Assistant
description:
Work tasks: The Role:
Dal’s Kitchen is looking for an organised and proactive Office & Food Safety Assistant to support our CEO and daily office operations while helping maintain our food-safety and BRCGS compliance systems. This is a varied position divided between office and executive-assistant duties and food-safety administration and internal auditing. It is suitable for someone who is highly organised, comfortable working with documents and systems, and interested in developing a career within food manufacturing and quality management. Office responsibilities: • Provide general administrative support to the CEO and wider management team. • Manage the CEO’s diary, appointments, meetings and reminders. • Organise meetings, prepare agendas, take minutes and follow up on agreed actions. • Maintain accurate customer, distributor and supplier information in the company CRM. • Prepare and issue customer invoices, credit notes and supporting documentation. • Monitor outstanding invoices and coordinate payment follow-ups. • Conduct research for the CEO, including suppliers, customers, distributors, competitors, logistics providers and new markets. • Prepare reports, presentations, spreadsheets and business correspondence. • Manage office documents, digital filing and confidential company information. • Coordinate travel arrangements, visits and external meetings when required. • Assist with purchasing, quotations and communication with service providers. • Support recruitment administration and employee-document management. • Monitor deadlines and ensure important actions are completed on time. Food-safety responsibilities • Support the implementation and maintenance of the Dal’s Kitchen food-safety and quality-management system. • Help maintain BRCGS, HACCP, food-safety, quality and operational records. • Plan, conduct and document scheduled internal food-safety and BRCGS audits. • Support external BRCGS and customer audits by preparing documentation, evidence and follow-up information. • Maintain the internal audit schedule and monitor completion against deadlines. • Record non-conformities and coordinate corrective and preventive actions with responsible team members. • Follow up corrective actions and verify that they have been completed effectively. • Assist with document control, including procedures, work instructions, forms and records. • Review production, cleaning, temperature, traceability, allergen and hygiene records for completeness. • Support traceability exercises, product-recall tests and other compliance checks. • Assist with supplier approval, specifications, certificates and food-safety documentation. • Monitor staff training records and help organise refresher training. • Report food-safety concerns, overdue actions and compliance risks to the CEO. • Help ensure the site remains prepared for announced and unannounced audits. BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9 provides a framework covering product safety, integrity, legality, quality and operational controls within food manufacturing; official certification is completed by an independent certification body, while this position would conduct internal audits and support certification audits.

We offer: What we offer
• A varied position with direct involvement in business operations and food safety. • The opportunity to work closely with the CEO and gain experience across multiple business functions. • Practical exposure to BRCGS, HACCP and food-manufacturing compliance. • Training and development relevant to the position. • The opportunity to grow with Dal’s Kitchen as the company develops. • Salary based on experience and qualifications.

Other requirements: • Väga hea eesti- ning inglise keele oskus, vene keel on eelis, kuid mitte kohustuslik. • Kehtiv B-kategooria juhiluba ja valmisolek regulaarseks reisimiseks Eestis ja välismaal. • Suurepärane suhtlemis-, läbirääkimis- ja esinemisoskus. • Tugev ärisuhete loomise võime ning praktiline, tulemustele orienteeritud tööstiil. • Hea MS Office’i kasutusoskus (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) ning kogemus CRM-i või müügiaruandluse tööriistadega. Positsioon sobib Sulle, kui oled: • Proaktiivne ja iseseisev algataja, kes suudab ise uusi kontakte luua ning oma müügitööd juhtida. • Struktureeritud, usaldusväärne ning valmidus töötama eesmärkide ja KPI-dega. • Kirg toidu vastu ning huvi Aasia köögi trendide vastu Eesti turul. • Meeskonnamängija, kes naudib koostööd kolleegidega müügi-, tootmis- ja turundusvaldkonnas.

title: Senior T24 Architect
description:
We are looking for an experienced Senior T24 Architect to shape the evolution of a large and complex Core Banking environment. You will define and guide the architecture of the Temenos T24 landscape, making sure that business capabilities, technology platforms and long-term strategic goals stay aligned.

You will work with business stakeholders, engineers, architects and external partners across multiple markets, providing architectural leadership over several initiatives and delivery streams. Your goal is to protect the stability and resilience of business-critical banking services while enabling platform modernisation and simplification.

Key Responsibilities:
 Shape and evolve the architecture roadmap for Temenos T24 and surrounding Core Banking capabilities, defining target-state architecture, principles and standards in line with business and technology strategy
 Provide end-to-end architectural leadership across complex initiatives, ensuring consistency, scalability and sustainability of the Core Banking landscape
 Translate business requirements into robust, implementable solutions, including integrations between Core Banking and payments, digital channels, lending, deposits, customer management and data platforms
 Identify interfaces, data flows and dependencies across applications, infrastructure and external services
 Evaluate architectural alternatives and make clear trade-offs between business value, delivery risk and technical complexity
 Drive modernisation and simplification of the Core Banking ecosystem, promoting API-first, event-driven and cloud-enabled patterns where appropriate
 Improve platform maintainability, testability and operability, and identify opportunities for reuse, automation and standardisation across markets and delivery teams
 Define functional and non-functional requirements for availability, security, performance, scalability, resilience and operability
 Guide architecture reviews to ensure alignment with enterprise standards and regulatory expectations, and maintain the architectural runway for sustainable delivery
 Assess architectural risks, technical debt and lifecycle concerns, and guide proportionate remediation
 Act as a trusted advisor for strategic Core Banking initiatives and technology investment decisions, communicating complex topics clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders
 Mentor architects and engineers, fostering collaboration and accountable decision-making within teams

Required Skills and Experience:
 Significant experience with Temenos T24 / Temenos Transact in architecture, solution design or senior engineering roles
 Deep understanding of Core Banking processes, platform capabilities and integration dependencies
 Proven record of leading architecture for large-scale transformation, migration or modernisation initiatives
 Experience working across multiple teams, products or markets in a complex enterprise environment
 Banking experience involving demanding availability, security, resilience and regulatory requirements

Please apply with your updated CV in English, that clearly demonstrates your skills and experience relevant to this role. We offer continuously, which means that we sometimes remove the assignments before deadline. If you are interested, we recommend that you apply immediately.

title: Automekaanikko
description:
Etsimme automekaanikkoa vakituiseen työsuhteeseen Paraisille! Asiakasyrityksemme on ollut toiminnassa jo yli kolmen vuosikymmenen ja he tarjoavat monipuolisesti palveluitaan liittyen ajoneuvojen huolto- ja korjauspalveluihin. Laadun takeena heillä on eri automerkkien sekä nykypäivän standardien monipuolinen ja pitkä tuntemus.

Tehtävässä keskityt tekemään ajoneuvojen huolto- ja korjaustehtäviä bensiini-, diesel-, hybrid- ja sähköautoille, on sitten kyseessä avustavat tai haastavemmat tehtävät. Työpäiviisi voi sisältyä esim. lisävarusteasennuksia, vikojen etsintää, alustatöitä, sähköistyksiä, moottorin korjauksia, vaihteistotöitä, jarrutöitä tai sitten yksinkertaisempia määräaikaishuoltoja kuten öljyjen ja suodattimien vaihdot sekä paljon muuta. Töitä tehdään asiakasyrityksen toimipisteellä ma-pe klo 8-16 ja 37,5h/viikko. Kuuntelemme palkkatoiveita, joten voit halutessasi esittää toiveesi hakemuksen yhteydessä.

Mitä toivomme sinulta?

\- B-ajokorttia ja SFS 6002 sähkötyöturvallisuuskorttia.

\- Olet suorittanut tehtävään soveltuvan koulutuksen ja sinulla on aikaisempaa työkokemusta vastaavista työtehtävistä sekä omaat monipuolisen merkkituntemuksen.

\- Tärkeänä pidämme myös kykyä sitoutua työhön, halua oppia ja omaksua uusia asioita, pitkäjänteisyyttä, ongelmanratkaisu- ja asiakaspalvelutaitoja, kädentaitoja, joustavuutta sekä itsenäistä, rehtiä ja ammattimaista työskentelyotetta.

Mitä tarjoamme sinulle?

\- Ammattitaitoisen yhteyshenkilön.

\- Palkanmaksun kahden viikon välein.

\- Lakisääteistä kattavamman työterveyshuollon ensimmäisestä päivästä alkaen.

\- Työn edellyttämän vaatetuksen, sekä tarvittaessa avustamme SFS 6002 sähkötyöturvallisuuskortin hankinnassa.

Paikka täytetään sopivan henkilön löydyttyä ja työt alkavat sopimuksen mukaan. Täytä hakemuksesi ohessa olevan linkin kautta ja kerro siinä mahdollisimman kattavasti itsestäsi, osaamisestasi sekä aikaisemmasta työkokemuksestasi. Kaikki yhteydenotot: Click Henkilöstöpalvelut Oy, Seniorikonsultti Riku Koski, puh. 0504110470, tiedustelut arkisin klo 9-16.
